messages:
maria: Quick sync — ran a continuous-batching sweep on canary with a new kernel routing tweak. Observed p99 climb (~180ms -> 280ms) under low qps when max_wait_ms=2 and max_batch_tokens=4096.
ray: ugh. was that the kernel fallback we added last week?
perf-bot: perf-check: profile_id=canary-2026-03-10-12:34, kernel_fallback=true, kv_hit_rate=0.87, tail_p99=279ms
sasha: interesting that kv_hit_rate is high but tail still spikes. could be eviction churn or small microbatch headroom causing more kernel switches.
maria: exact sequence: requests with seq_len~512 often form tiny microbatches (2-3 tokens) -> scheduler flushes at max_wait_ms -> fallback to fallback-kernel (fp16->int8 path) triggers extra memcpy+relaunch.
ray: can you paste the config you used?
maria: sure:
```
scheduler: 
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
  max_wait_ms: 2
  max_concurrent_microbatches: 8
  kernel_routing: {prefers_fast_kernel: true, fallback_on_timeout: true}
```
jordan: small ask: what was the client arrival pattern? microbursts vs steady?
maria: bursty — short bursts every 200ms, worker util ~40% avg. tail worse during bursts.
sasha: hypothesis: when bursts hit, KV cache misses for prefix chunks cause extra kernel handshake latency, pushing those batches over p99. Also low max_wait_ms gives less time to accumulate compatible tokens so more fallbacks.
ray: try raising max_wait_ms to 6 and increasing max_batch_tokens to 8192 for a canary, keep other knobs same. should smooth tail but may slightly increase median.
maria: queued a canary now with those params + an experiment to prefer the slower kernel only when batch_size_tokens>1024.
perf-bot: canary-deploy: canary-2178-03, config_override={max_wait_ms:6,max_batch_tokens:8192,prefer_threshold:1024}. started 12:41UTC
ray: also add kv metrics: per-prefix eviction_rate, rebuild_latency, and kernel_switch_count to the trace.
sasha: and add a heatmap for per-request microbatch_size vs latency (p50/p95/p99) so we can see the elbow.
maria: will do. quick reproduction command I used:
```
perf run --workload=burst_200ms --seq=512 --duration=10m --profile-out=/tmp/canary.prof
```
jordan: if this smooths p99 but increases p50 by ~5-10ms that's acceptable, but if p99 stays above 250ms we need to revert.
ray: also check GPU kernel queue depth and memcpy stalls in nvprof traces — sometimes the 'fallback kernel' label hides a memcpy + kernel combo.
sasha: noted. I'll pull nvprof for the failing traces.
maria: next steps: 1) collect added kv + kernel_switch metrics for the canary (in flight) 2) nvprof samples for two p99 traces 3) run controlled replay with perf run reproducer and compare with baseline.
ray: can we set an alert on kernel_switch_count spike > 5/s per instance? that would catch regressions quickly.
maria: yep will add that alert to the canary dashboard.
perf-bot: metric-alert created: kernel_switch_spike_canary (threshold=5/s)
jordan: timeline? can we have initial results in ~90m?
maria: aiming for 60-90m. will report back with a short table. :thumbsup:
ray: thanks — if this looks promising we should roll to dedicated pool with slightly higher max_wait to reduce unit cost via better batching.
sasha: and document the tradeoff in the runtime tuning guide: example profiles for bursty vs steady workloads and recommended max_wait_ms ranges.
maria: adding notes to the PR. will post results here when ready.
